input.question: How was the NASA mission Magellan able to map the Venusian surface so quickly?
input.ground_truth: Venus’ day is 243 earth days long. Magellan orbited Venus every 3 hours or so. That means that during a single Venusian day, the probe circled the planet almost 2000 times. I don’t know what you mean by quickly, but it took almost an entire earth year to get that 96%, for what it’s worth.

Question: How was the NASA mission Magellan able to map the Venusian surface so quickly?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine Venus is like a big, cloudy cake that you can’t see through. The Magellan spaceship was like a special airplane that flew around this cake (Venus) and took lots and lots of pictures. It used something called "radar," which is like bouncing invisible balls off the cake to see what shape it has, even through the clouds.

Because Magellan flew around Venus many times and took pictures from different sides, it could put all the pictures together like a puzzle. That’s how it made a map of Venus really fast!
